name: Functional test of an RSFQ digital-SQUID ADC with TFF and cumulative counters (AIST HSTP Nb process) at 4.2 K in a pulse-tube cryocooler
plain_name: Run a superconducting digital chip at 4.2 K to check that its logic works
description: A wire-bonded SFQ chip (digital-SQUID modulators, majority logic, toggle flip-flop and cumulative counters) is cooled to 4.2 K in a two-stage closed-cycle pulse-tube cryostat with a vibration-damping stage; separate DC bias rails from a HYPRES current source, clock through a bias-tee on RF-shielded coax, outputs amplified and checked on an oscilloscope and logic analyser.
keywords: Run a superconducting digital chip at 4.2 K to check that its logic works

sources.citation: Experimental Demonstration of a Superconductor SFQ-Based ADC for High-Frequency Signal Acquisition (Ucpinar et al., arXiv:2510.14191, 2025)

requirements.rationale: The niobium SFQ circuit is operated at 4.2 K.
Bias currents, clock and output signals are wired to the chip.
High-frequency inputs and the clock are delivered on RF-shielded coaxial lines.
Optional: at least three separate DC bias rails (DC/SFQ, SFQ/DC, main power) were used.
Optional: the cryocooler sample space is under vacuum (vacuum level monitored); a liquid-helium dip test would not need it.
Optional: the source chose a closed-cycle system instead of liquid-helium immersion.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
